evidence: Flora of North America / Hodgson Bixaceae treatment: Amoreuxia has two dimorphic fertile stamen sets
A. wrightii species description: distal filaments 5-10 mm with yellow anthers; proximal filaments 11-17 mm with usually dark-red anthers
2010 review explicitly treats former Cochlospermaceae within Bixaceae under APG III
Lunau et al. 2017 explicitly figures Verbascum phoeniceum (Scrophulariaceae) with within-flower heteranthery
Current Kew taxonomy retains Verbascum phoeniceum in Scrophulariaceae
Scrophulariaceae.timing_guard: Evidence postdates the 2010 review and is used only as an independent family representative, not as reconstruction of Table S1.

evidence: Darwin 1877 reports several Mollia species with long outer and short inner stamen cohorts carrying differently coloured pollen and explicitly examined M. lepidota and M. speciosa
Müller 1883 independently summarizes differently coloured anthers/pollen in several Mollia species
Current Kew/Smithsonian taxonomy places Mollia in Malvaceae
Malvaceae.reason_open: The 2010 review states that Malvaceae had only one reported heterantherous species, while the historical evidence covers multiple Mollia species; exact single-species identity is not uniquely identified.
